olivia: Heads up — kicked off the quarterly access attestation dry run. Ran an owner lookup for service accounts and flagged several unexpected KMS grants crossing prod -> staging. Dropping findings here so we can triage.

jae: Can you paste the exact query/command you used? I can run a scoped diff across projects.

olivia: Query I used (quick local dump):
```sql
SELECT svc.name, svc.owner, grant.key_id, grant.grantee_project
FROM service_accounts svc
JOIN kms_grants grant ON svc.id = grant.svc_id
WHERE grant.grantee_project != svc.home_project
  AND svc.last_used > now() - interval '90 days';
```
And the CLI to inspect a single key's grants (GCP):
```bash
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY --location=global --keyring=kr --project=prod-project
# then diff with: gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY --project=staging-project
```

security-bot: AccessScan report generated: 23 service accounts with >=1 cross-project KMS grant. Top offenders: svc-ingest, svc-analytics, svc-deployer. Report: https://internal/reports/attest-1712348001 :eyes:

marcus: If those grants are real we should do a canary rollback. Remove elevated bindings from staging first, validate jobs, then scheduling prod remediations. Also need to correlate IAM/grant audit logs to the actor who made the change before removing.

luis (audit): I pulled the audit logs for the last 60 days for the top 5 keys. Here's the gist (Stackdriver/GCP audit):
```text
protoPayload.methodName=SetIamPolicy
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=deployer-ci@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
resourceName=projects/prod-project/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/KEY
request.time=2024-09-03T14:22:11Z
```
Two grants were created by a partner-integrations service account during a rollout spike — looks like an automation bug.

jae: Good catch. I'll scope a revoke script that targets only the partner integrator principal and leaves other bindings. Plan: run in staging, smoke test pipelines, then open a PR for prod change.

jea (typo note): btw, if revoke touches running deployers we'll fallback to the backup key per runbook.

olivia: Correct — fallback plan: switch affected pipelines to backup-key-2024-09-01 (documented in runbook link). If smoke tests fail, rollback the revoke and investigate automation. @security-bot can you add an incident tag and page the oncall if the staging revoke causes >5% job failures?

security-bot: incident tag added: #attest-1712348001. Will page sec-oncall if failures > 5% in the next 30m post-change.

marcus: Also let's add a short-lived policy to block cross-project grants from the partner integrator until we fix automation. We can enforce with an org policy + deny rule or a pre-commit TF gate.

luis (audit): I'll draft the deny rule and attach the PoC. Also scheduling a quick attestation sync at 10:30 to align owners and reviewers.

jae: I'll post the scoped revoke PR and link the smoke test logs here when done. ETA ~2h.

olivia: Thanks all. Quick checklist: 1) jae runs staging revoke (scoped) 2) run smoke tests + monitor (security-bot watch) 3) if green, PR for prod revoke + org policy PoC 4) followup postmortem on automation bug.

marcus: :thumbsup:

luis (audit): I'll capture evidence for the attestation export and mark affected owners for manual confirmation.

olivia: Meeting invite sent for 10:30. Keeping thread for updates.
